record.paper_title: (E,E′N) and (E,E′NN) Experiments at NIKHEF, Mainz and JLab and Open Problems in One- and Two-Nucleon Emissions
record.original_question: Do nucleons bound inside nuclei undergo medium-dependent modifications of their electromagnetic form factors, and if so, how can those modifications be disentangled from conventional nuclear effects such as meson-exchange currents, isobar configurations, and final-state interactions in polarization-transfer observables? A related open direction is whether more precise super-ratio measurements, including analyses beyond 4He and on nuclei such as 16O, can separate genuine in-medium structure changes from reaction-model ambiguities.

evidence.quote: However, it has proven to be a very difficult task to disentangle changes of the nucleon structure from other conventional nuclear effects, such as meson-exchange currents, isobar configurations and FSI, because the nucleon form factors of a bound nucleon are not observable.
A proposal for a similar analysis on 16O is under discussion.
Measuring the components of the induced (transfer) polarization, on the other side, gives important information about possible medium modification of the nucleon electromagnetic form factors.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the quasi-elastic electron-scattering reactions A(e⃗,e′p⃗)B on nuclear targets A (e.g., A = 4He, 16O), in which a longitudinally polarized electron knocks out a proton whose recoil polarization components Px′ (transverse) and Pz′ (longitudinal, along momentum transfer) are measured. Define the polarization-transfer ratio R(A) = Px′/Pz′ and the super-ratio

  S(A) = [Px′/Pz′]_A / [Px′/Pz′]_{1H},

i.e., the ratio measured on the nucleus normalized to that for elastic e p scattering on a free proton (1H(e,e′p)). For a free proton, R is proportional to the ratio of the proton electric to magnetic Sachs form factors GE^p/GM^p; for a bound proton, conventional reaction effects (meson-exchange currents (MEC), isobar/Δ configurations, and final-state interactions (FSI)) plus possible medium-induced changes of the bound nucleon's electromagnetic form factors all contribute.

Problem. (a) Determine whether nucleons bound inside a nucleus possess electromagnetic form factors that differ from their free-space values, in a manner observable through polarization-transfer observables in A(e⃗,e′p⃗)B reactions. (b) Provide a theoretical and experimental framework that unambiguously separates such genuine in-medium form-factor modifications from the conventional contributions of meson-exchange currents, isobar configurations, and final-state interactions in the components of the induced (transferred) recoil polarization. (c) In particular, decide whether high-precision measurements of the super-ratio S(A) extended beyond A = 4He to nuclei such as A = 16O can distinguish genuine medium modifications from reaction-model ambiguities, and identify the specific kinematic regimes and observables in which this separation is achievable.
artifact.status_search_result: JLab polarization-transfer measurements on 4He (PRL 94, 072303 (2005); follow-up 2008) found deviations from relativistic distorted-wave calculations consistent either with medium-modified form factors (quark-meson coupling models) or with strong charge-exchange final-state interactions, leaving the interpretation ambiguous. Subsequent theoretical and experimental work (e.g., reviews through ~2019) continues to debate this disentanglement, and an analogous 16O measurement remains a proposed/ongoing direction. The question therefore appears still open.

status_evidence.title: Polarization Transfer in 4He(e,e'p)3H: Is the Ratio GE/GM Modified in the Nuclear Medium?
status_evidence.snippet: Measured ratio of polarization-transfer coefficients differs from a fully relativistic calculation, favoring either medium-modified proton form factors (QMC) or strong charge-exchange FSI.
status_evidence.claim: The interpretation of the 4He super-ratio data is not unique, reflecting an open disentanglement problem.

status_evidence.title: Medium Modifications from 4He(e,e'p)3H
status_evidence.snippet: Follow-up JLab measurement of the polarization-transfer double ratio in 4He probing possible medium modifications of the proton form factor.
status_evidence.claim: Continued experimental effort indicates the question remains under investigation.

status_evidence.title: Review on Nucleon Electromagnetic Form Factors (H. Gao)
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews status of medium modifications and the ambiguity with FSI and other reaction mechanisms.
status_evidence.claim: As of the review, no unambiguous separation of medium modifications from conventional effects has been achieved.
